title: Data Fusion of Synthetic Query Variants With Generative Large Language Models

live_model.evidence: Sec. 3.1: 'we rely on OpenAI's gpt-4o. At the time of our experiments, this identifier points to the model version gpt-4o-2024-05-13'; 'fixed seed and a temperature parameter of 0.0'

prompt.location: Sec. 3.1, 'Prompt template for strategies P-1, P-2, and P-3' (role line, 100-query request, optional description/narrative and example queries)
prompt.note: P-3 examples come from TREC Web track 2013/2014 topics 201, 251, 263, 266, 296 (UQV100 variants).

claim.metric: nDCG@10 of RRF-fused BM25 rankings over P-2 query variants, Core17
claim.location: Table 1, block Core17, row d P-2, column NDCG@10

data.source: TREC Core17 (NYT, LDC2008T19), Core18 (WaPo), Robust04 (Disks 4&5), Robust05 (AQUAINT) need NIST/LDC licences; topics/qrels public; code and generated queries at https://github.com/breuert/sigirap24

notes: Retrieval side needs a BM25 index of the licensed corpus and RRF (k=60); the released query-variant sets allow a direct comparison of the LLM stage. Whole study cost the authors ~$22.50.

resolution.plan: nDCG@10 requires BM25 retrieval over the New York Times Annotated Corpus (LDC2008T19, footnote 7), which is licence-gated, and the other three collections (Washington Post, Disks 4&5, AQUAINT) are agreement-gated as well, so the reported number cannot be recomputed from public inputs. Only the LLM stage (P-2 variants for the 50 Core17 topics, prompt in Sec. 3.1, gpt-4o-2024-05-13 at temperature 0 with a fixed seed) can be re-run and compared with the released variant sets at github.com/breuert/sigirap24, which is not the paper's number.
